Clinical_Definition_and_Measurement: Biological sex recorded at hospital admission.
Patient chronological age in years at the time of the index ERCP.
Body mass index calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared. Categorized according to Chinese adult standards.
Serum total bilirubin concentration measured from the most recent venous blood sample obtained prior to the index ERCP.
Serum total cholesterol concentration from the most recent pre-procedural fasting lipid panel.
Total serum calcium level measured prior to the index ERCP.
Maximum diameter of the common bile duct measured on intraoperative retrograde cholangiographic images during full contrast opacification.
Documented clinical history of acute cholangitis prior to or at presentation for index ERCP.
Placement of endoscopic nasobiliary drainage tube at the conclusion of the index ERCP.
Endoscopic papillary large balloon dilation performed using a dilation balloon with diameter ≥ 12 mm, either alone or following EST.
Presence of a periampullary diverticulum within a 2-3 cm radius of the major duodenal papilla identified during duodenoscopy.
Documented medical diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (type 1 or type 2) or ongoing anti-diabetic medication therapy.
Presence of concurrent gallstones in the gallbladder verified by pre-procedure ultrasonography, CT, or MRCP.
Documented prior clinical episodes of acute pancreatitis according to Atlanta classification criteria.
History of surgical cholecystectomy performed prior to the index ERCP.

Permissible_Values_Encoding: 1 = Single stone (1); 2 = Two stones (2); 3 = Multiple stones (≥ 3)
Clinical_Definition_and_Measurement: Total number of stones identified in the common bile duct on intraoperative cholangiography before extraction.
Maximum diameter of the largest common bile duct stone measured on intraoperative cholangiography.

Chinese_Name: 内镜乳头括约肌切开术
Clinical_Definition_and_Measurement: Performance of endoscopic sphincterotomy at the major duodenal papilla during the index ERCP.
Angle formed between the distal common bile duct trajectory and the proximal bile duct axis on standardized intraoperative cholangiography.
Reappearance of stones in the common bile duct verified by abdominal imaging (ultrasonography, CT, MRI/MRCP) or repeat ERCP occurring at least 6 months after complete stone clearance.
